key_insight: Intensity-modulated photoluminescence spectroscopy (IMPLS) measures perovskite charge-carrier lifetime at a defined operating injection level, and can separate lifetime from interfacial charge-transfer effects.
engineering_relevance: The method provides a practical, operating-condition diagnostic for perovskite thin films and solar cells, helping benchmark device quality and identify interface-limited losses.
method: Use frequency-domain IMPLS instead of conventional time-resolved PL.
Measure under operating or one-sun-equivalent illumination to obtain lifetime at a specific injection level.
Apply a transfer function for perovskite/transport-layer stacks to disentangle charge transfer from interface recombination.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that thin-film IMPLS lifetimes match steady-state photoluminescence, and that in devices IMPLS reveals a third frequency absent in IMVS, enabling direct lifetime extraction.
watch_item: In stacked devices the IMPLS response is more complex, so interpretation requires a dedicated transfer-function analysis to avoid confusing charge transfer with recombination.
paper_title: Operando Charge Carrier Dynamics by Intensity-Modulated Photoluminescence: From Perovskite Thin Films to Solar Cells
